neighbours.label: The head noun of an economics technical term (public-good result, producer surplus, deadweight loss), vs the same nouns in everyday use
fire: Economists often cite the free-rider result when explaining why parks are underfunded.
A price ceiling reduces consumer surplus for some buyers and creates a shortage.
The tax creates a deadweight loss that neither buyers nor sellers recover.
Under perfect competition, economic profit falls to zero in the long run equilibrium.
The second welfare theorem result says any efficient allocation can be reached with transfers.
In the diagram, the area above the supply curve is the producer surplus of the market.
The Coase theorem result holds only when transaction costs are negligible.
Ricardo's comparative advantage result explains why both countries gain from trade.
quiet: Doctors often cite the test result when explaining why the patient stayed overnight.
The shop sold its surplus stock of umbrellas at half price in the summer.
She felt a deep loss when her old dog died last winter.
The bakery made a small profit at the weekend market in the long run of rain.
The second exam result was much better than the first one for her class.
In the drawing, the area above the river is a green field with sheep.
The final match result was announced over the loudspeakers at noon.
Her advantage in the race came from a fast start off the line.

predictions: Fire items 0.2-0.6 on the head noun (result, surplus, loss); everyday uses under 0.1. Card is mixed (physics, digits in code), so a fail is plausible.
